question: Feature pack v2 was NOT promoted for the transformer (see feature_pack_v2_gate.json). But the XGBoost baseline resolved its features through feature_columns(df), which included any v2 column that happened to be present in the frame. Did the rejected v2 pack silently move the published baseline, and are the committed baseline numbers internally consistent?
verdict: TWO FINDINGS, the second CORRECTED on 2026-07-28 (see committed_report_reconciliation). (1) The silent-promotion mechanism was REAL but its measured effect is NEGLIGIBLE: mean OVERALL PPR MAE delta of v2 minus v1 is +0.0014 across 2023-2025, i.e. v2 is marginally WORSE and well inside noise. (2) The two committed reports disagreed because of a feature-set change, NOT data vintage -- the same implicit-on-presence bug, one generation earlier (snap_pct, added ~16 h after baselines.json was generated). Proof: naive_last4 is byte-identical across the two reports while xgboost differs on every row, so the data cannot have changed. Both reports have since been regenerated on one vintage and now agree. A third finding fell out: XGBoost's own seed jitter (~0.012 OVERALL, up to ~0.047 on the smallest cell) is comparable to or larger than every feature and vintage effect examined here, so the seed is now recorded too.

measured.method: Same walk-forward folds (train < S, test == S) through the existing eval harness, both entrants in ONE harness call so they see byte-identical rows. No tuning; nothing selected on these numbers.
measured.reading: Sign flips across seasons and the mean is +0.0014 on a metric whose season-level SE in this project is ~0.028. The v2 columns did not meaningfully help or hurt the tabular baseline.

committed_report_reconciliation.note: Neither feature set reproduces the committed OVERALL xgboost rows, and the two committed reports disagree with EACH OTHER on the same model/season/test-set.
committed_report_reconciliation.conclusion_SUPERSEDED: Original reading: 'data vintage dominates, the feature set is not the main driver'. THIS WAS WRONG and is corrected below. It was inferred from residual magnitudes alone without checking which models moved.
committed_report_reconciliation.conclusion: CORRECTED 2026-07-28. The baselines-vs-bakeoff gap is NOT data vintage -- it is a feature-set change, one generation earlier than the v2 pack. Decisive evidence: between the two committed reports, naive_last4 is BYTE-IDENTICAL on 0/15 rows while xgboost differs on 15/15. naive_last4 is computed from the same lagged data, so any change of data vintage would have moved it too. It did not move; therefore the data was the same and only the tabular feature resolution changed. Dating it: baselines.json was generated 2026-07-10 06:25 UTC, roughly 16 h before commit 978f9fc added snap_pct, so it ran on 38 feature columns against today's 40. That is the SAME implicit-on-presence bug this audit fixed, caught one generation earlier than the v2 pack. Only the bakeoff-to-now half is attributable to data vintage.
committed_report_reconciliation.second_correction: The original text called the 0.017 report-to-report gap 'an order of magnitude larger than the feature effect'. That overstated it. XGBoost subsamples (subsample/colsample_bytree), and refitting on byte-identical data with seeds 0-3 spans ~0.012 OVERALL PPR MAE and up to ~0.047 on the smallest per-position cell. So 0.017 is roughly 1.4x the model's own seed jitter, not an order of magnitude above anything. Dropping the snap_pct lags moves 2023 OVERALL by only -0.0026. Practical consequence: several effects this project has chased are at or below XGBoost's seed noise, so the report now records xgb_seed alongside the feature set and data vintage -- two reports are not comparable at this resolution unless all three match.

what_changed.mechanism: feature_columns(df, feature_set) is now versioned and explicit, mirroring how the transformer resolves feature_set per artifact. Registry: BASELINE_FEATURE_SETS = {v1: (), v2: (lag4/lag8_air_share, is_indoor, team_pass_att_last4)}.
what_changed.default: v1, FROZEN. Chosen because v1 is the set every committed baseline report was generated with, so the reported walk-forward comparisons keep meaning what they say. Opting into v2 is now a deliberate, recorded act.
what_changed.entrant_naming: XGBBaseline(feature_set='v2').name == 'xgboost_v2', so a non-default run can never land in a report under the baseline's own name.
what_changed.pinned: tests/test_features.py pins the v1 column list literally AND in order (colsample_bytree makes column order part of the fit), so a new column added to build_features cannot silently rejoin the baseline's inputs.

scope.does_not_re_litigate: The feature-pack-v2 gate FAILED and stays failed (feature_pack_v2_gate.json). This audit fixes the baseline's feature resolution and the record; it is not a re-run of that experiment and selects nothing.
scope.resolved: RESOLVED 2026-07-28. Both reports were regenerated in one pass on a single data vintage with the frozen v1 feature set, and now agree on xgboost OVERALL (4.44854 mean). naive_last4 and xgboost came back bit-identical across the two regeneration runs at full float precision, which is what proves no data shift mid-exercise (the same check the FPv2 gate used). Reports now carry xgb_feature_set, xgb_seed and a data_vintage block (feature_rows plus a sha256 per source parquet), so this class of silent incomparability is detectable rather than inferable after the fact.
scope.largest_change: One cell moved more than 0.05: bakeoff.json xgboost/2023/QB, 6.0561 -> 6.1072 (+0.0510). Investigated rather than waved through -- seeds 0-3 on identical data span 6.0602-6.1073 on that exact cell (range 0.047, sd ~0.024), and it is the smallest cell in the report (n=663), so the move sits inside the model's own seed spread. Every OVERALL row moved <= 0.021. Recorded because a reader comparing old and new reports will otherwise see an unexplained 0.05.
